parts: Please review /papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/research-overview/01_RESEARCH_OVERVIEW_GOALS_AND_TASKS_20261018.md and  symmetries/research-progress/01_RESEARCH_TASK_TRACKER_20261018.md, and continue with S04/T03. Please update the summary file in the summary folder when you're done.
I’ll read the overview, tracker, and repository guidance, then continue S04/T03 and update the summary with the results.

The tracker leaves S04/T03 waiting for uniform residual and anchor estimates. S03’s newer arithmetic result gives us a fixed-box estimate to test. I’ll check how its constants, anchors, and cutoff corrections behave as height grows; the S04 Gaussian average alone does not control isolated collisions.

A local residual bound transfers uniformly to short windows at every height in the stated sector. The long-range continuation has a concrete problem: paying each cutoff change separately produces an error budget that grows exponentially as time shrinks. I’m quantifying that loss and separating the available anchor error bound from the positive anchor margin still needed for exclusion.

The uniform local increment bound is below 0.090111 at the sector’s opening point. The independent cutoff-transition budget already exceeds 148 there and diverges as time shrinks. I’ll record this as a local transfer result and a failure of that specific payment rule. Signed, coherently matched cutoff corrections remain open.

The derivation, source checks, and 192/256-bit runs pass. A separate reviewer also replayed the result and caught an interval-handling issue in the reusable helper; it is fixed and checked. I’m now saving the note and review, marking T03 complete at its scoped gate, and updating the summary and tracker.

Completed S04/T03’s bounded deliverable and updated the [summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/summary/01_SYMMETRY_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_SUMMARY_20261019.md) and tracker.

- Proved a uniform local residual-increment bound: \(<46.679e^{-b_*/t}\).
- Showed that independent cutoff-transition payments grow exponentially, ruling out that specific continuation rule.
- Passed 192/256-bit checks and a separate internal replay.

Coherent global transfer and positive physical anchor margins remain open.
Please continue with S05-T1
I’ll review S05’s source enclosures and test one existing consumer for a compatible, measurable bottleneck, then record the fit decision and update the summary.

The S01 consumer uses a shifted complex contour, so it cannot use S05’s narrower real near-zero enclosures. I’m also checking S06’s real endpoint calculation to see whether its error budget offers a compatible use.

S06’s current endpoint calculation also uses no real source-cell range bounds: it evaluates endpoints directly and pays the remainder with analytic integral bounds. About 81.8% of its remainder allowance comes from the sixth-derivative integral bound. I’m checking one remaining possibility before closing the fit decision: S05’s fused polynomial formula may improve S01’s existing complex quadrature.

There is a compatible candidate: factoring the retained source polynomial while preserving S01’s existing contour and exponential grouping. A one-coefficient check reduced its quadrature radius by about 0.0736% at both precisions. That is roughly 0.0047% of the complete value allowance if the other coefficients and errors stay unchanged. I’ll record it as the S05-T2 candidate, with the original parity-Taylor route parked and the full consumer benefit still untested.

S05-T1’s fit decision is complete. I’ll retain the compatible polynomial-factoring candidate for T2, document the rejected real-parity handoffs, and update the summary and tracker. The separate 192/256-bit replays agree; no full coefficient setup or physical consumer comparison has been run.

S05-T1 is complete. Selected polynomial factoring in S01’s shifted coefficient acquisition as the next candidate; the real parity-Taylor handoffs do not fit the inspected callers.

The tested coefficient’s error radius decreased **0.07361%**, confirmed at 192/256 bits and by separate replay. Full consumer benefit remains untested.

Updated the [summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/summary/01_SYMMETRY_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_SUMMARY_20261019.md), overview and tracker. S05-T2 is **Ready** under the explicitly documented acquisition-route update.
Please continue with S05-T2
I’ll run the selected coefficient-acquisition comparison, carry its errors through the complete consumer, and update the summary and tracker with the result.

The comparison will use all 51 coefficients, the same physical domain, and the existing closed-cell cover. I’ll compare the expanded, factored and exponentially grouped formulas, then test a hybrid that keeps each coefficient with its matching midpoint and radius. Any hybrid result will carry the cost of all three acquisitions.

The review added a useful attribution check: compare the new hybrid against a hybrid of the two existing formulas. That will separate any benefit from polynomial factoring from the benefit of simply mixing old alternatives. The unchanged Taylor and tail terms still limit how much the complete error can fall.

The full comparison changes the ranking from the one-coefficient test. Exponential grouping is weaker at coefficient 0 but much tighter at coefficient 2, making it the strongest pure formula overall. Against the stronger hybrid of the existing formulas, adding polynomial factoring lowers the complete error allowances by about 0.0092%, 0.0078% and 0.0082%. The reported physical margin and coverage remain unchanged.

Independent full replays at both precisions agree with the acquisition and consumer results. The smaller approximation-error allowances do not produce a consistent increase in the physical margin, and the hybrid requires extra acquisition work. I’m recording T2 as complete for the error reduction and closing this fixed-box comparison.

S05-T2 is complete for the error-reduction objective. The full 51-coefficient comparison reduced complete added-error allowances by approximately **0.0092%, 0.0078%, and 0.0082%** against the stronger hybrid baseline.

Separate internal 192/256-bit replays passed. No consistent margin, cost, or coverage advantage was established.

Updated the [summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/summary/01_SYMMETRY_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_SUMMARY_20261019.md), task tracker, research notes, and review.
Please continue with S06-T1
I’ll review S06-T1 and the latest handoff, carry out the next research step, and update the summary and tracker.

S06-T1 asks whether a completed transverse observation gives a new estimable remainder. I’m testing the next transverse order: its source correction must be formed before integration, and its full observation must retain the mixed terms. The key check is whether it remains controlled at the physical energy scale near a collision.

The second-order completion converges, but it fails the proposed collision test: its centered current is strictly positive at a nondegenerate collision, where physical energy is zero. I’m documenting that scoped obstruction and checking the full formulas, boundary terms, and control sources before updating the tracker.

The checks confirm the obstruction on a complete convergent control source, with its own constants. The exact formulas retain all four product terms and the lower boundaries. I’ll mark S06-T1 complete for this scoped result; S06-T2 remains waiting for an independently estimable term. The separate internal review is finishing.

S06-T1 is complete with a scoped negative result: the second-order completed current stays positive at an actual collision, so its positivity cannot supply the proposed exclusion test. **S06-T2 remains Waiting** for a different independent estimate.

Exact checks, source controls, and separate same-model internal review passed.

Updated the [summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/summary/01_SYMMETRY_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_SUMMARY_20261019.md), tracker, research note, and review.
Please continue with S06-T2
I’ll review S06-T2’s entry conditions and the T1 findings, then look for an independent estimating term that can support the bounded comparison. I’ll update the summary and tracker with the result.

T1 left a useful alternative: subtracting the higher-jet term gives a residual that vanishes at a collision. It can be estimated directly from the complete source without assuming the old Laguerre sign. I’ll test it on the existing pilot and compare its paid lower bound for physical energy with the direct bound from the same data.

The first replay gives a clear result: the new residual signs 60 of the 64 fixed cells, while the direct first-jet bound certifies all 64. On each of those 60 cells, the current gives a weaker energy bound. I’ll finish the second-precision replay and review, then close this fixed-pilot attempt without refining the failed cells.

Both precision runs agree: the residual test remains inconclusive on four cells, while the direct bound covers all 64. The review also confirms a narrower result for this method: extracting an energy bound from the scalar residual cannot outperform the direct norm bound on the same Cartesian jet data. I’m saving the records and updating the summary to distinguish the finished comparison from its failed benefit gate.

S06-T2’s bounded comparison is complete; **its benefit gate failed**. At both 192/256 bits, the new residual certifies 60/64 cells; four remain inconclusive. Direct certification covers all 64 and gives stronger bounds.

Separate same-model internal review passed. This fixed-pilot attempt is closed; the broader S06 estimate remains open.
